A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from them then took the unwanted material along into 80 other wells: wells B5, B6, B7, B8, B9, B10, B11, B12 and 72 more in slot 1.
findings.fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 109 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids afterwards with a fresh tip each.

findings.title: A used tip carried reagent (well A1 in slot 5) into 7 wells it was never meant for
findings.explanation: At line 86 the tip touched the liquid in tubes A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1 and B2 in slot 3 while it still carried reagent (well A1 in slot 5) from an earlier step (this line did it 7 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches. The protocol never transfers that liquid into these wells on purpose, so it was not meant to be there. If the wells hold different samples, each now holds a little of another. Liquid was later taken out of the affected wells, and the unwanted material went along into 21 other wells: wells G4, G5, G6, G7, G8, G9, G10, G11 and 13 more in slot 1.
findings.fix: Use a fresh tip for each well at line 86. If one tip must serve many wells, dispense from above the liquid (for example `well.top()`) so that the tip never touches what is already in the well.

findings.explanation: At line 57 the tip touched the liquid in tube A2 in slot 3 while it still carried water (tube C1 in slot 3) from an earlier step. Liquid was later taken out of the affected wells, and the unwanted material went along into 83 other wells: wells A1, A2, B5, B6, B7, B8, B9, B10 and 74 more in slot 1; well A1 in slot 5.
findings.fix: Use a fresh tip for each well at line 57. If one tip must serve many wells, dispense from above the liquid (for example `well.top()`) so that the tip never touches what is already in the well.

findings.title: (proposed) A tip that had been in a sample went into a reagent
findings.explanation: At line 88 the tip touched the liquid in well A1 in slot 5 while it still carried bsa (tube A1 in slot 3) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, and the protocol never transfers that liquid into this well on purpose. A reagent is shared: the master mix, the enzyme or the primer in that well goes into every reaction on the plate. A tip that has been in one sample leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so a sample carried into a reagent well turns up in every well that reagent reaches, and a no-template control can no longer be trusted. Liquid was later taken out of the affected wells, and the unwanted material went along into 82 other wells: wells B3, B4, B5, B6, B7, B8, B9, B10 and 74 more in slot 1.
findings.fix: Use a fresh tip for each sample at line 88, or add the reagent to the wells first, while the tip is clean, and the samples afterwards with a fresh tip each.
